purpose: Diagnostic rubric for the AI Coach. Consumed by the assess/score LangGraph nodes. This is a COACHING rubric (assessed against), NOT a teaching curriculum.

proficiency_levels.name: Novice
proficiency_levels.meaning: Knows the term; needs step-by-step guidance; no real project use.

proficiency_levels.name: Advanced Beginner
proficiency_levels.meaning: Uses it in tutorials/toy projects; misses edge cases.

proficiency_levels.name: Competent
proficiency_levels.meaning: Ships it in real projects; makes deliberate trade-offs.

proficiency_levels.name: Proficient
proficiency_levels.meaning: Designs it; debugs failure modes; optimizes cost/latency.

proficiency_levels.name: Expert
proficiency_levels.meaning: Sets patterns for others; handles novel/ambiguous cases; mentors.

assessment.notes: Rank competencies by weight; probe high-weight/low-coverage first. Adapt follow-ups to answers. Stop when weighted coverage of critical+high reaches threshold or the user opts to see results.

scoring.calibration: Validate judge vs a small human-labeled sample (Cohen's kappa); tune prompt until agreement is acceptable.

competencies.name: Chunking strategies
competencies.sample_question: Design a RAG system over a company's legal contracts. How would you chunk the documents, and where do retrieval failures usually come from?

level_anchors.2: Naive fixed-size chunking, no overlap consideration.
level_anchors.4: Structure/semantic-aware chunking tuned to the corpus; reasons about overlap, metadata, and how chunking affects recall.

competencies.name: Embeddings & embedding models
competencies.sample_question: How do you choose an embedding model, and how do you know it's good enough for your data?

level_anchors.2: Uses a default embedding model without evaluation.
level_anchors.4: Selects by domain/latency/cost, evaluates retrieval quality, considers fine-tuned or domain embeddings.

competencies.name: Vector databases (Qdrant/Pinecone/Weaviate/pgvector)
competencies.sample_question: Which vector store would you pick and why, and how do metadata filters change your design?

level_anchors.2: Knows one store, basic top-k similarity.
level_anchors.4: Chooses per requirements, uses metadata filtering, understands index types and trade-offs.

competencies.name: Hybrid search & re-ranking
competencies.sample_question: Pure vector search returns irrelevant chunks. What do you add to improve relevance?

level_anchors.4: Combines lexical + dense (hybrid), adds a re-ranker, measures the lift.

competencies.name: Retrieval evaluation
competencies.sample_question: How do you measure whether your retrieval is actually working?

level_anchors.4: Uses recall/precision/hit-rate on a labeled set, separates retrieval vs generation failures (e.g., RAGAS).

competencies.name: Graph RAG (Neo4j)
competencies.sample_question: When would a knowledge graph beat plain vector RAG?

level_anchors.4: Uses graph relationships for multi-hop/structured queries where vector similarity falls short.

competencies.name: When NOT to use RAG
competencies.sample_question: When is RAG the wrong tool, and what would you do instead?

level_anchors.4: Weighs long-context, fine-tuning, or tool-calling alternatives depending on the problem.

competencies.name: Function/tool calling
competencies.sample_question: Walk me through how you expose tools to an LLM and make sure it calls them correctly.

level_anchors.2: Basic single tool, hopes the model calls it.
level_anchors.4: Clear tool schemas/descriptions, validates args, handles tool errors and retries.

competencies.name: ReAct & planning loops
competencies.sample_question: How does an agent decide its next action, and how do you keep the loop from running forever?

level_anchors.4: Implements bounded reasoning loops with step limits, planning, and termination conditions.

competencies.name: LangGraph (state machines, checkpointing, HITL)
competencies.sample_question: Why model an agent as a graph? How do checkpointing and human-in-the-loop fit in?

level_anchors.4: Designs state schemas, uses checkpointers for resumability, subgraphs for modularity, and HITL interrupts.

competencies.name: Multi-agent patterns (CrewAI)
competencies.sample_question: When do multiple agents beat one, and what breaks when you add them?

level_anchors.4: Uses multi-agent only when roles/parallelism justify it; manages coordination, cost, and error propagation.

competencies.name: Agent memory
competencies.sample_question: How does your agent remember things within and across sessions?

level_anchors.4: Separates short-term (thread) vs long-term memory, summarizes/retrieves, manages the context budget.

competencies.name: MCP (build/consume servers)
competencies.sample_question: What is MCP and when would you build a server for it?

level_anchors.4: Builds/consumes MCP servers to expose tools/data in a standard, secure, reusable way.

competencies.name: Failure-mode handling
competencies.sample_question: Your agent sometimes loops or calls the wrong tool. How do you make it reliable?

level_anchors.4: Step limits, validation, fallbacks, retries, observability, graceful degradation.

competencies.name: Eval design & golden datasets
competencies.sample_question: How do you know your LLM app is actually good?

level_anchors.4: Builds golden datasets, defines metrics tied to the use case, runs systematic evals.

competencies.name: LLM-as-a-judge
competencies.sample_question: How would you use an LLM to grade another LLM, and what goes wrong?

level_anchors.4: Rubric-grounded judge, controls verbosity/position/self-preference bias, calibrates against humans.

competencies.name: Eval frameworks (RAGAS/DeepEval/Promptfoo/LangSmith)
competencies.sample_question: What tooling do you reach for to evaluate a RAG or agent pipeline?

level_anchors.4: Uses appropriate frameworks and integrates them into the workflow.

competencies.name: Regression testing
competencies.sample_question: You change a prompt. How do you make sure you didn't break anything?

level_anchors.4: Automated regression suite in CI over a fixed dataset with thresholds.

competencies.name: Offline vs online eval
competencies.sample_question: What's the difference between evaluating before and after deployment, and why do both?

level_anchors.4: Offline for iteration + online (production signals, A/B, user feedback) for reality.

competencies.name: Measuring agent quality
competencies.sample_question: How do you evaluate a multi-step agent, not just a single response?

level_anchors.4: Evaluates trajectory, tool-use correctness, task completion, and cost/latency.

competencies.name: Tokenization & context windows
competencies.sample_question: What actually happens when your prompt gets too long?

level_anchors.4: Reasons about tokens, truncation, cost, and context-window management strategies.

competencies.name: Sampling params (temperature, top-p)
competencies.sample_question: When do you change temperature/top-p and why?

level_anchors.4: Tunes deliberately for determinism vs creativity per task.

competencies.name: Structured outputs / JSON mode
competencies.sample_question: How do you get reliable, schema-valid JSON out of a model?

level_anchors.4: Uses structured-output/JSON modes with schemas and validation + retries.

competencies.name: Streaming
competencies.sample_question: Why and how would you stream tokens to a user?

level_anchors.4: Streams for perceived latency, handles partial/aborted streams.

competencies.name: Multi-provider APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic/Groq)
competencies.sample_question: How do you keep your code from being locked to one LLM provider?

level_anchors.4: Abstracts providers, handles differences, enables routing/fallback.

competencies.name: Model selection & trade-offs
competencies.sample_question: How do you pick which model to use for a given task?

level_anchors.4: Routes by quality/latency/cost per task with evidence.

competencies.name: Cost/token awareness
competencies.sample_question: How do you keep LLM costs under control at scale?

level_anchors.4: Monitors token cost, caches, compresses context, routes to cheaper models.

competencies.name: System prompt design
competencies.sample_question: How do you design a system prompt for a consistent agent persona and behavior?

level_anchors.4: Structured, testable system prompts; separates role, constraints, tools, examples.

competencies.name: Few-shot & role prompting
competencies.sample_question: When do examples help and when do they hurt?

level_anchors.4: Chooses representative examples, watches token cost and overfitting to format.

competencies.name: Context-window management
competencies.sample_question: Your context keeps overflowing. How do you decide what to keep?

level_anchors.4: Budgets context, summarizes, retrieves selectively, prioritizes by relevance.

competencies.name: Tool/function description quality
competencies.sample_question: An agent misuses a tool. How do you fix it via the tool's description/context?

level_anchors.4: Treats tool descriptions as an interface: precise, examples, constraints, measured iteration.

competencies.name: Prompt templating & versioning
competencies.sample_question: How do you manage prompts across a codebase so you can reproduce behavior?

level_anchors.4: Templated, versioned prompts tied to code, with change tracking.

competencies.name: Hallucination reduction via prompting
competencies.sample_question: What prompting techniques reduce hallucination, and what are their limits?

level_anchors.4: Grounding, citations, 'say I don't know', constrained output; knows prompting alone isn't enough.

competencies.name: FastAPI + streaming/WebSockets
competencies.sample_question: How do you serve an LLM app that streams responses to many users?

level_anchors.4: Async streaming over SSE/WebSocket, backpressure, connection handling.

competencies.name: Caching (prompt/response)
competencies.sample_question: Where can caching help in an LLM pipeline?

level_anchors.4: Prompt/response caching, embedding cache, semantic cache with invalidation.

competencies.name: Model routing & fallbacks
competencies.sample_question: A provider goes down mid-request. What happens?

level_anchors.4: Automatic fallback/routing across providers with degradation, not a hard failure.

competencies.name: Latency & cost optimization
competencies.sample_question: Your app feels slow and expensive. Where do you look first?

level_anchors.4: Profiles TTFT/throughput/cost per stage, optimizes model/caching/context deliberately.

competencies.name: Rate-limit & concurrency handling
competencies.sample_question: How do you handle provider rate limits under load?

level_anchors.4: Queues, backoff, concurrency caps, per-key budgeting.

competencies.name: Deployment
competencies.sample_question: How do you take a prototype to a deployed service?

level_anchors.4: Containerized, config/secrets management, health checks, real deploy target.

competencies.name: Tracing (LangFuse/LangSmith/Helicone)
competencies.sample_question: Responses got worse yesterday. How do you find out what changed?

level_anchors.4: Traces per-request spans, inputs/outputs, tokens, latency; searchable and comparable.

competencies.name: Token/cost monitoring
competencies.sample_question: How do you track cost per request and per feature over time?

level_anchors.4: Per-request token/cost metrics, dashboards, alerts on anomalies.

competencies.name: Prompt versioning with code
competencies.sample_question: How do you reproduce a past behavior of your app?

level_anchors.4: Prompts versioned with code so any past behavior is reproducible.

competencies.name: Logging I/O for debugging
competencies.sample_question: What do you log for an LLM feature and why?

level_anchors.4: Structured I/O logging balanced with privacy/PII and cost.

competencies.name: CI/CD for LLM apps
competencies.sample_question: What runs in CI for an LLM app that wouldn't for a normal service?

level_anchors.4: Eval/regression gates on prompt/model changes in CI.

competencies.name: async/await & concurrency
competencies.sample_question: You're calling an LLM API 500 times in a batch. How do you structure that for speed and resilience?

level_anchors.4: Async with concurrency limits, backoff, timeouts.

competencies.name: Type hints & Pydantic
competencies.sample_question: How do you validate and model structured data in Python?

level_anchors.4: Typed models with Pydantic validation at boundaries.

competencies.name: Testing (pytest, mocking LLM calls)
competencies.sample_question: How do you test code that depends on an LLM API?

level_anchors.2: Calls the real API in tests.
level_anchors.4: Mocks/records LLM calls, deterministic tests, fixtures.

competencies.name: Packaging & dependency management
competencies.sample_question: How do you manage dependencies and environments for a Python project?

level_anchors.4: Locked deps, virtual envs, reproducible builds (uv/poetry).

competencies.name: Clean architecture / project structure
competencies.sample_question: How do you structure a growing LLM app so it stays maintainable?

level_anchors.4: Layered/modular structure, separation of concerns, clear interfaces.

competencies.name: Error handling, retries & timeouts
competencies.sample_question: An external call flakes intermittently. How do you handle it?

level_anchors.4: Typed errors, retries with backoff, timeouts, circuit breaking.

competencies.name: Prompt-injection defense
competencies.sample_question: Your agent reads user-supplied documents and can call tools. What could go wrong?

level_anchors.4: Treats external content as untrusted, isolates instructions, limits tool permissions.

competencies.name: Jailbreak resistance
competencies.sample_question: How do you keep users from making your agent misbehave?

level_anchors.4: Layered defenses, refusal handling, monitoring for abuse.

competencies.name: Guardrails
competencies.sample_question: How do you constrain what your agent is allowed to output or do?

level_anchors.4: Input/output guardrails, allow-lists, validation layers.

competencies.name: PII handling
competencies.sample_question: How do you handle personal data flowing through an LLM app?

level_anchors.4: Minimizes, redacts, controls retention, aware of compliance.

competencies.name: Red teaming
competencies.sample_question: How do you proactively find your agent's weaknesses?

level_anchors.4: Systematic adversarial testing before shipping.

competencies.name: When to fine-tune vs RAG vs prompt
competencies.sample_question: When would you fine-tune instead of RAG or better prompting?

level_anchors.2: Thinks fine-tuning is the default fix.
level_anchors.4: Clear decision framework: prompt -> RAG -> fine-tune, based on the problem.

competencies.name: LoRA / QLoRA
competencies.sample_question: How would you fine-tune a model cheaply?

level_anchors.4: Understands LoRA/QLoRA trade-offs, hardware/cost implications.

competencies.name: Dataset curation
competencies.sample_question: What makes a good fine-tuning dataset?

level_anchors.4: Quality, diversity, labeling, dedup, and eval split discipline.

competencies.name: Evaluating fine-tuned models
competencies.sample_question: How do you know your fine-tune actually improved things?

level_anchors.4: Compares against baseline on held-out evals, watches for regressions.
